16.0.0.en: After the death of the two sons of Aaron, "Nadab and Abihu," who offered strange fire on the altar of God and not the holy fire that came down from heaven (ch. 10), the Lord spoke to Moses and gave him the law of the great Day of Atonement, on which Aaron the high priest would enter the Holy of Holies to make atonement for himself and for the people.

16.1.0.en: God warned Aaron, by the mouth of Moses, against entering the holy place, meaning the Holy of Holies, and passing the veil, which is the curtain dividing the sanctuary from the Holy of Holies, and standing before the mercy seat, that is, the cover of the Ark of the Covenant, where God appears in His glory in a cloud, whether what is meant is the natural cloud that appears in the sky or the thick incense that Aaron offers before the Ark of the covenant of God, so that its appearance is like a cloud. The high priest's entry into the Holy of Holies takes place once every year, on the Day of Atonement. If he enters at any other time, he dies, out of respect for the presence of God and as a showing of His justice, which cannot be seen except through the blood of Christ, which is offered only on the Day of Atonement before the Ark of the Covenant.

16.1.1.en: The fear of God protects you from falling into many sins, and if you fall, you hasten to repentance. If God in His love allows you to see His temple and His altar and to partake of His Holy Mysteries, do not forget His justice and the fear of Him, so that you may pray with reverence and live in purity.

16.2.s.en: (2) Preparing the sacrifices of the Day of Atonement

16.2.0.en: Here he mentions the sacrifices that Aaron offers for himself and for the priests, which he buys from his own money, as a declaration that all need the redemption of Christ, whether priest or people. These sacrifices that he prepares are:

16.2.1.en: 1- A young bullock, which he offers as a sin offering to make atonement for his sins and those of the priests.

16.2.2.en: 2- A ram for the burnt offering, that God may be pleased with him and the priests.

16.3.0.en: After Aaron has offered the morning burnt offering as set out in (Ex 29:38-42, Num 28:3-8), he goes to a place in the tabernacle of the congregation to wash his whole body and to change his splendid priestly garments for garments like those of the rest of the priests, which are:

16.3.1.en: 1- Linen breeches, which are an undergarment worn on the waist and covering the thighs.

16.3.2.en: 2- A linen coat, which resembles a long robe reaching to the feet and covering the arms.

16.3.3.en: 3- A linen girdle, which is a belt tied around the waist with its two ends hanging down in front toward the feet.

16.3.4.en: 4- A linen miter, that is, a cap, which is a simple head covering like what the priest wears today (the tailasan). The high priest changes his garments and puts on ordinary priestly garments so that he may be humbled and know that he needs atonement to be made for him like the rest of the priests and the people.

16.4.0.en: As for the sacrifices that Aaron offers for the people, which are from their own money, they are:

16.4.1.en: 1- Two kids of the goats as a sin offering; one is slaughtered and the other is let go, as we will explain in this chapter, and they are to make atonement for the sins of all the people.

16.4.2.en: 2- A ram for the burnt offering, that God may be pleased with the people.

16.5.0.en: Aaron brings near the bullock of the sin offering, which he will offer for his sins and those of his sons the priests, and stands it before the door of the tabernacle of the congregation at the bronze altar, and confesses his sins and those of his sons the priests before God, that He may forgive them, in a general confession that was written down among the Jews. The priest of the New Testament too, in the Divine Liturgy, offers repentance for his own sins before the sins of the people, which is a declaration of the need of all for the salvation of Christ the Redeemer.

16.6.0.en: The high priest stands the two goats offered for the sins of the people before the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, with their faces toward the west, that is, toward the sanctuary, and casts lots between them to choose one of them for the Lord, that is, to offer it as a sacrifice to God, and the other for Azazel, that is, to let it go far away outside the camp into the wilderness. The first goat signifies the shedding of the blood of Christ for the forgiveness of the sins of those who believe in Him, and the second goat signifies Christ's removal of our sins from us and setting them far away, that is, freeing us from them, for the word Azazel comes from separating and removing. The goat to be offered as a sacrifice is tied with a red thread, and the goat of Azazel with a scarlet thread, that is, a dark red, to distinguish them.

16.7.0.en: Aaron presents the goat of the sin offering that will be slaughtered before God, and slaughters it after slaughtering the bullock.

16.8.0.en: As for the second goat, on which the lot fell to be for Azazel, the high priest stands it before God to make atonement for the people, that is, to bear their sins and remove them by sending it to Azazel, as a symbol of separating the sins of the people from them.

16.8.1.en: If Christ has redeemed you by His blood and has removed your sins from you, and you have received this in the two sacraments of confession and Holy Communion, then take care to live pure and reject all sources of evil.

16.9.0.en: Aaron himself slaughters the bullock of the sin offering, because by it he makes atonement for himself and for the priests his sons.

16.10.0.en: Aaron takes the golden censer particular to this day, which is large in size, and puts in it burning coals, that is, glowing charcoal from the bronze altar, and enters the sanctuary and takes his hands full of sweet incense beaten small, that is, well ground so that it burns easily and its sweet fragrance spreads, and puts the incense in a special golden vessel. It is noted that he took a large quantity of incense to put in the large censer, so that the incense would spread inside the Holy of Holies like a great white cloud covering the Ark of the Covenant and the mercy seat, so that Aaron does not see it, because it is the great throne of God, which no one can look at because of its greatness and the fear it inspires. Then he enters the Holy of Holies carrying the censer in his right hand and the incense vessel in his left. He enters sideways, that is, not looking toward the cover of the Ark, and places the censer on a stone set on the ground, and then puts into it the abundant incense that is in the vessel, so the incense rises like a mist and covers the whole place, and he senses the presence of God and cannot see the mercy seat.

16.11.0.en: Aaron goes out from the Holy of Holies to the sanctuary and takes the vessel containing the blood of the bullock from one of the priests assisting him, and then enters the Holy of Holies a second time and sprinkles with his finger, that is, sprinkles some of the blood, on the cover, which is called the throne or the mercy seat, and at which the two cherubim, who represent divine justice, look. This blood signifies the blood of Christ, which fulfills the requirements of divine justice on behalf of mankind and so saves us.

16.11.1.en: Then he sprinkles some of the blood that is in his left palm with the finger of his right hand on the ground before the Ark, as a declaration that we have no entrance to the Father except by the blood of Christ the Redeemer (Eph 2:18). He sprinkles toward the east side of the Ark of the Covenant and the cover, which faces the veil and the sanctuary, because the place of the Holy of Holies is to the west of the sanctuary and to the west of the tabernacle of the congregation. So Aaron enters from the veil, that is, from the east, toward the Ark of the Covenant that is in the west, so that the east side of the Ark is in front of him, and he sprinkles on it; thus the phrase "toward the east" means the east of the Ark.

16.11.2.en: Wonderful is God in His humility; around Him the angels stand in great fear, yet He condescends to dwell in our midst so that we may take courage and draw near to Him, and He makes atonement for us by His blood so that we may be accepted, indeed loved and brought close to His embrace. May we offer repentance with reverence, so that we may enjoy His love and live in reassurance.

16.12.0.en: Aaron slaughters the goat on which the lot fell and offers it to God, takes some of its blood and enters the sanctuary and then the Holy of Holies, and sprinkles some of its blood once on the cover and seven times on the ground before the Ark, as he did in the rite of sprinkling the blood of the bullock. This time he offers the blood on the cover to make atonement for the people, and on the ground so that the people may have access and entrance to God, that He may be their God and they may be His people. This is the third time that Aaron enters the Holy of Holies.

16.13.0.en: Because of the sins of the people, the house of God, that is, the contents of the tabernacle of the congregation, is defiled; therefore he mixes the blood of the bullock with the blood of the goat and sprinkles it on all the contents of the sanctuary, and likewise the contents outside the sanctuary, so the tabernacle of the congregation is cleansed, for the blood of Christ cleanses His people and His Church. This shows that our sins defile the Church of God and anger Him, but by faith and repentance we obtain our purity.

16.13.1.en: Because of the people's defilement of the tabernacle of the congregation, there is an opinion that the seven times that the priest sprinkles before the Ark on the ground are to cleanse the Holy of Holies, which became unclean because of the sins of the people, and then he sprinkles on the rest of the contents of the tabernacle of the congregation so that the whole place may be clean.

16.14.0.en: While the high priest is entering the Holy of Holies, there is no one, of the priests or the people, either in the sanctuary or in the tabernacle, since all need atonement to be made for them. And Aaron here signifies Christ, by whom alone atonement is made for us.

16.15.0.en: Here he stresses the sanctification of the contents of the sanctuary and the tabernacle, and in particular the altar of incense, which is in front of the veil, that is, in front of the Holy of Holies. He takes some of the blood of the bullock and the blood of the goat, mixed together, and anoints the four horns of the altar, and then sprinkles with his finger seven times on the altar, to declare that Christ the Redeemer, by His blood and ascending as incense for us before the Father, is our strength, which appears in the horns of the altar, which represent strength, and seven times, that is, the fullness of sanctification and cleansing. And just as he cleansed the altar of incense, he cleanses the rest of the contents of the tabernacle by sprinkling them with blood.

16.16.0.en: After finishing the sanctification of everything in the tabernacle of the congregation by means of the blood of the bullock and the goat, he brings the second goat, which is called the goat of Azazel, and stands it before God at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, that is, he declares that it is presented to God.

16.17.0.en: Aaron comes forward as the representative of the people and lays his hands on the head of the live goat, that is, the goat of Azazel, and confesses the sins of all the people in a prayer that the Jews had prepared to declare their repentance and ask God's forgiveness. This is a clear symbol of the sacrament of confession, in which the sins of those who confess are transferred to Christ, who bears them for them and forgives them. Then he gives this goat to the one he meets, which is either the first person he meets or a particular person who comes forward and meets Aaron, and this is the more common opinion; this person is most likely one of the priests, and he takes the goat and goes with it to the wilderness and lets it go alive there.

16.17.1.en: The following is noted about the two goats:

16.17.2.en: 1- The slaughtered goat is a symbol of Christ who died on the Cross for us, and the second goat, which is let go alive in the wilderness, is a symbol of the risen Christ who gave us new life by the Resurrection.

16.17.3.en: 2- The first goat makes atonement by its blood in the sanctuary, far from the eyes of the people, while the second goat is let go alive before the eyes of all, to reassure them that their sins have been forgiven. The first is a secret relationship with God, and the second is a public relationship and visible worship before all.

16.17.4.en: Drive away your evil thoughts by repeating the Psalms or occupying yourself with anything spiritual. It also helps you to change your place, to declare before God your rejection of the evil thought, so that He supports you with His help to cut sin off at its roots and stop its growth into any other forms in word or deed.

16.18.0.en: After the high priest lets the goat of Azazel go, he enters a special place in the tabernacle of the congregation and takes off the simple linen garments in which he offered the sacrifices and offerings of atonement, and then washes his whole body, as an expression of his purification from the sins connected with the sacrifices and offerings of atonement; then he puts on his full priestly garments, that is, the splendid ones, to offer the additional sacrifices of this day, followed by the evening sacrifice.

16.19.0.en: After the high priest bathes and puts on his full garments, he offers burnt offerings for himself and for all the people. For after sins have been removed by the sacrifices and offerings of atonement, he can offer burnt offerings of a sweet savor before the Lord, who is pleased with him and with his people.

16.19.2.en: 1- A ram as a burnt offering for Aaron, mentioned in (v. 3).

16.19.3.en: 2- A ram as a burnt offering for the people, mentioned in (v. 5). In addition to the additional burnt offerings mentioned in detail in (Num 29:7-11), which are:

16.19.4.en: 3- A bull, and with it three tenths of fine flour mingled with oil and half a hin of wine, which he pours on it when offering it.

16.19.5.en: 4- A ram, and with it two tenths of fine flour mingled with oil and a third of a hin of wine.

16.19.6.en: 5- Seven lambs of the first year as burnt offerings, and with each one of them one tenth of fine flour mingled with oil and a fourth part of a hin of wine.

16.19.7.en: In addition to a sin offering, which is a kid of the goats.

16.20.0.en: Aaron offers the fat of the sin offering, which is:

16.20.1.en: 1- The fat of the bullock that Aaron offered as an atonement for himself (v. 3).

16.20.2.en: 2- The fat of the sacrificed goat offered as an atonement for the people (v. 5).

16.20.3.en: 3- The fat of the goat of the sin offering offered as an additional sacrifice and mentioned in (Num 29:10, 11). The altar mentioned here is the bronze altar that is in front of the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, on which the fat of the sacrifices is offered because it is the richest part of them, and so it is offered to God.

16.21.0.en: The goat of Azazel is considered unclean because it bears the sins of the people; therefore the one who takes it and lets it go in the wilderness must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and remain outside the camp until the evening to be cleansed and be permitted to enter the camp.

16.21.1.en: Offer repentance for any sin you fall into, or any stumbling place you go to, or any clinging to wicked people who helped you toward sin, and let there be for you a period of repentance, that is, prayers and confession, so that you may be permitted to partake of the Holy Sacraments.

16.22.0.en: In the case of any sin offering, after its fat is offered, the priest eats its flesh and takes its skin. But on the Day of Atonement, because the sin offerings are offered for the priests themselves and for all the people, no one eats of the flesh of the sin offerings, whether the bullock or the goat offered for the people or the additional goat; rather, they bring out the flesh of these sacrifices, their skins and their dung, and burn them outside the camp, just as Christ was crucified and suffered outside the camp.

16.23.0.en: The one who burns the flesh, skin and dung of the sin offerings outside the camp becomes unclean because they bear sins, and therefore he must:

16.23.3.en: 3- Remain outside the camp until the evening, and then enter it after he has obtained his purity; this is like the one who let go the goat of Azazel.

16.23.4.en: After that the high priest offers the evening burnt offering as is customary every day, by the same rite as the morning burnt offering that was offered at the beginning of this day, as mentioned in (Num 29:12).

16.24.0.en: God concludes His words about the Day of Atonement by asking the following of His people:

16.24.1.en: 1- Humbling themselves and repenting of sins, which is accompanied by fasting.

16.24.2.en: 2- Freeing themselves from material work to concentrate on the meaning of atonement.

16.24.3.en: 3- Observing the Day of Atonement on the tenth day of the seventh month every year until Christ came and accomplished atonement for our sins on the Cross.

16.24.4.en: 4- All the worshipers receive forgiveness of their sins on this day, whether the native, who is of Jewish origin, or the stranger, that is, the Gentile who became a Jew and lived with the children of Israel.

16.25.0.en: He mentions that the Day of Atonement is a day of rest, so he calls it a sabbath, that is, a day of rest, but it need not fall on a Sabbath; it can be any other day of the week. Along with rest, he stresses the necessity of fasting, which he expresses as humbling oneself before God.

16.26.0.en: The high priest anoints the one who will succeed him, who is his firstborn, as high priest after him, and he is the most important person on this day because he himself offers the sacrifices, assisted by the rest of the priests. He fills his hand, that is, he offers the sacrifices and carries them with his hands, and takes care to wear linen garments as a declaration of his humility, as we mentioned.

16.27.0.en: The high priest sanctifies and anoints everything in the tabernacle of the congregation with the blood of the sacrifices of atonement, as a symbol of Christ, who sanctifies His Church and all who believe in Him.

16.28.0.en: Moses and Aaron obeyed all the commands of the Lord, and so they kept the Day of Atonement every year.

16.28.1.en: The Church offers special worship on Good Friday every year and offers fasting and humility on the Friday of every week, so it is an opportunity for you to remember the mercies of God, who removed your sins by His redemption, so that you thank Him, praise Him and contemplate His love.
